result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_d_separator()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Check if a set of nodes d-separates two others in a directed acyclic graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_d_separator()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Check if a set of nodes d-separates two others in a directed acyclic graph. title: >- [Graph.is_d_separator()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check if a set of nodes d-separates two others in a directed acyclic graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of nodes d-separates two others in a directed acyclic graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L57823-L57919){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_d_separator( x, y, z, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is d-separator](../assets/graphs/is-d-separator.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A causal graph: smoking (teal) causes tar, tar causes cancer (violet), and smoking also causes yellow fingers. Left: conditioning on tar (outlined) blocks the only path from smoking to cancer, so is_d_separator returns True. Right: with nothing conditioned on, the chain smoking, tar, cancer (accent) is open, so smoking and cancer are dependent and is_d_separator returns False." width="100%"} In a causal diagram or Bayesian network (a DAG whose edges point from causes to effects), d-separation reads conditional independence off the graph: if `z` d-separates `x` from `y`, then `x` and `y` are independent given `z` in every probability distribution that respects the graph. A path between them is *blocked* by `z` when it passes through a chain or fork node in `z`, or through a collider (a node with both path edges pointing into it) that is not in `z` and has no descendant in `z`. `z` d-separates `x` and `y` when every path is blocked. This is the basis of choosing adjustment sets in causal inference and of testing a causal model against data. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name} : Nodes, or lists of nodes, as IDs or labels. [y]{.doc-parameter-name} : Nodes, or lists of nodes, as IDs or labels. [z]{.doc-parameter-name} : The conditioning nodes (a node, a list, or an empty list). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if `z` d-separates `x` from `y`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not a directed acyclic graph, a node does not exist, or the three sets are not disjoint. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The check is a "Bayes ball" style search (Shachter, 1998) from `x` that moves backward to parents and forward to children, passing through a node in `z` only as a collider and through a collider only when it is an ancestor of `x` or `z` (a sufficient criterion for an open collider path). It visits each node at most once in each direction, so it runs in $O(V + E)$ time, as NetworkX's `is_d_separator` does. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Smoking causes tar, tar causes cancer, and smoking also causes yellow fingers. Smoking and cancer are dependent, but conditioning on tar blocks the only path between them: ::: {#1424dfe1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["smoking", "tar", "cancer", "fingers"]) g.add_edges([("smoking", "tar"), ("tar", "cancer"), ("smoking", "fingers")]) g.is_d_separator("smoking", "cancer", []), g.is_d_separator("smoking", "cancer", "tar") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (False, True) ``` ::: ::: Conditioning on a common effect (a collider) opens a path. Talent and luck are independent, but become dependent among people who are known to be successful: ::: {#1b2f822a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} h = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["talent", "luck", "success"]) h.add_edges([("talent", "success"), ("luck", "success")]) h.is_d_separator("talent", "luck", []), h.is_d_separator("talent", "luck", "success") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
